summary: The main functions of an operating system and the features of single-user, multi-user, single-tasking, multitasking, real-time, network and batch processing operating systems.

blocks.content: System software that **manages the computer's hardware and software resources**, provides a **user interface**, and provides a **platform** on which application software runs.

Without an OS, every application would need to contain its own code for controlling the screen, keyboard, disks and memory. The OS does this **once, for all programs**, and shares the hardware between them safely.

flowchart TB
  U[User] <--> UI[User interface]
  UI <--> APP[Applications]
  APP <--> OS[Operating system kernel]
  OS <--> DRV[Device drivers]
  DRV <--> HW[Hardware: CPU, RAM, disks, devices]
blocks.caption: The OS sits between the applications and the hardware

blocks.title: What happens when a computer is switched on (booting)
items: The **BIOS / UEFI** firmware in ROM runs a **power-on self-test (POST)** of the hardware.
It finds the storage device that holds the OS and runs the **bootstrap loader**.
The bootstrap loader copies the OS **kernel** from secondary storage into **RAM**.
The OS starts its services and drivers and shows the **log-in screen / user interface**.

theory.title: The main functions of an operating system

items.title: Memory management
items.content:
- **Allocates** RAM to each program and its data when it starts, and **frees** it when the program closes.
- **Protects** memory so one program cannot overwrite another program's data.
- Uses **virtual memory** (part of the disk used as RAM) when main memory is full.

items.title: Processor (process) management
items.content:
- Decides **which process uses the CPU** and for how long (**scheduling**).
- Switches between processes so that many programs appear to run at once (**multitasking**).
- Handles **interrupts** — signals from hardware or software that need the CPU's attention.

items.title: File management
items.content:
- Creates, names, opens, saves, copies, moves and deletes files.
- Organises files in a **hierarchical folder (directory) structure**.
- Records **where** each file is stored on the disk and controls **access rights** to files.

items.title: Input/output and peripheral management
items.content:
- Communicates with devices through **device drivers**.
- Uses **buffers** to hold data travelling between fast and slow devices.
- Uses **spooling** to queue print jobs so the CPU does not wait for the printer.

items.title: Security and user management
items.content:
- **User accounts**, **log-in** with user names and passwords / biometrics.
- **Access rights** (read, write, execute) to files and folders.
- Firewall, security updates, logging of activity.

items.title: User interface
items.content:
- Lets the user communicate with the computer: **GUI**, **command line**, menu, touch, voice.
- Displays error and status messages.

items.title: Error handling
items.content: - Detects errors (a device not responding, a program crashing) and reports or recovers from them without stopping the whole system.

items.title: Loading and running software
items.content: - **Loads** applications from storage into memory, starts and stops them, and provides services (system calls) they can use.

blocks.title: The OS at work — printing a document
blocks.content:
1. The user clicks **Print** (user interface).
2. The OS **loads** the printer driver and places the document in the **print queue** (spooling).
3. While the printer prints, the **processor manager** lets the user continue typing (multitasking).
4. Data is sent to the printer through a **buffer** (I/O management).
5. If the printer runs out of paper, an **interrupt** is sent and the OS shows an error message (error handling).

blocks.title: Memory management terms
rows: Giving a program the memory it needs
Preventing a program from accessing another program's memory
Using part of secondary storage as an extension of RAM
Memory divided into fixed-size blocks (pages) moved between RAM and disk
The computer slows down because pages are swapped too often

blocks.content: Name the function **and** say what the OS does: not just "memory management", but "*memory management — the OS allocates RAM to each program and stops programs from overwriting each other's memory*".
An OS that allows **only one user** to use the computer **at a time**. Examples: Windows 11 or macOS on a personal laptop, Android on a phone.

An OS that allows **many users** to use the computer's resources **at the same time**, usually from different terminals or over a network. Each user has an account, and the OS shares processor time, memory and storage between them. Examples: **UNIX / Linux servers**, mainframe OSs (z/OS), Windows Server.

flowchart LR
  T1[Terminal 1] --> S[Mainframe or server running a multi-user OS]
  T2[Terminal 2] --> S
  T3[Terminal 3] --> S
  T4[Terminal 4] --> S
blocks.caption: A multi-user system shares one powerful computer between many terminals

blocks.title: Single-user vs multi-user OS
rows: All resources belong to one user
CPU time, memory and storage are shared fairly between users (**time-sharing**)
Simpler — one account at a time
Must **keep users' data separate**; strong authentication and access rights
Linux / UNIX servers, z/OS, Windows Server

blocks.title: Single-user can still have many accounts
blocks.content: A family laptop may have several **user accounts**, but only **one person** is logged in and using it at a time, so it is still a **single-user** OS in this classification.
An OS that can run **only one program (task) at a time**. The next task starts only when the current one finishes. Examples: MS-DOS, the OS of a simple calculator or embedded device.

An OS that can run **several programs at the same time**. The processor switches between tasks very quickly, giving each a short **time slice**, so they **appear** to run simultaneously. Examples: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android.

CPU:  | Music | Browser | Editor | Music | Browser | Editor | Music | ...
time  --------------------------------------------------------------->
The switching happens many times per second, so the user sees all three programs running.
blocks.caption: Time slicing — one CPU, three tasks (each block is one time slice)

blocks.title: How multitasking works
items: Each running program is a **process** held in memory.
The **scheduler** gives each process a **time slice** of CPU time (e.g. round-robin), often based on **priority**.
When the time slice ends (or an interrupt occurs), the OS **saves the state** of the process (registers, program counter) and **loads** the next one — a **context switch**.
The cycle repeats many times per second.

blocks.title: Single-tasking vs multitasking
rows: CPU is idle while the task waits for input/output
CPU is kept busy — another task runs while one waits
Needs more memory — every running task is held in RAM
Must close one program to open another
Switch between programs; background tasks (downloads, music)
Full CPU power for one task
Each task may run slower as the CPU is shared

blocks.content: On a single-core processor, multitasking only **looks** simultaneous — the CPU runs **one** instruction stream at a time and switches quickly. A **multi-core** processor can really run tasks in parallel.

An OS that **processes inputs and responds within a guaranteed, very short time** (a deadline), so that it can **control** a physical process as it happens. Used in embedded and safety-critical systems.

items.title: Features of an RTOS
items.content:
- **Guaranteed response time** — inputs are processed within a fixed deadline (milliseconds or less).
- **Deterministic / predictable** — the same input always takes the same time to handle.
- **Priority-based, pre-emptive scheduling** — the most urgent task interrupts less urgent ones.
- **Continuously monitors sensors** and uses **feedback** to control actuators.
- **Very reliable**, runs non-stop for long periods; often has **fail-safe** / backup systems.
- **Small, efficient** and usually has a **minimal or no user interface**; often stored in ROM (embedded).

items.title: Hard and soft real-time
items.content:
- **Hard real-time** — missing a deadline is a **system failure** and may be dangerous: airbag control, aircraft autopilot, pacemaker, anti-lock brakes.
- **Soft real-time** — missing a deadline only **reduces quality**: video streaming, online games, ticket booking.

blocks.content:
flowchart TB
  S[Sensor reads value] --> P[RTOS processes the input within the deadline]
  P --> A[Actuator acts]
  A --> E[Physical process changes]
  E --> S
blocks.caption: An RTOS controls a process using a feedback loop

blocks.title: Real-time systems
blocks.content:
| System | Why real time is needed |
|---|---|
| **Car airbag** | Must inflate within about 30 ms of a crash being detected |
| **Anti-lock brakes (ABS)** | Must release and reapply the brakes many times a second |
| **Aircraft autopilot / flight control** | Must react instantly to changes in speed, height and wind |
| **Hospital patient monitor** | Must sound an alarm immediately when heart rate is dangerous |
| **Industrial robot / traffic lights** | Must perform actions at exact times |

blocks.title: RTOS vs general-purpose OS
rows: Good average performance and ease of use

blocks.content: An OS designed to **manage a network and its shared resources** — users, files, printers, applications — usually running on a **server** that client computers connect to. Examples: **Windows Server**, **Linux** server distributions (Ubuntu Server), UNIX, Novell NetWare (historic).

items.title: Features of a NOS
items.content:
- **User account management** — creates accounts and groups and **authenticates** users when they log in.
- **Authorisation / access rights** — controls which users can read, change or delete each shared file, folder and printer.
- **File and printer sharing** — central storage that all authorised users can reach; print queues for network printers.
- **Security** — firewall, encryption, logging of activity, enforcing password policies.
- **Centralised backup** and software updates for the whole network.
- **Remote access** and administration of client computers.
- **Network services** — e.g. DHCP, DNS, e-mail, web hosting.
- Supports **multi-user** access at the same time.

blocks.title: How a NOS implements user account management (exam answer)
blocks.content: The NOS provides **authentication and authorisation** mechanisms (1) so that only **authorised users** can access network resources (1). It **verifies each user's identity** with a user name and password when they log in (1) and **assigns appropriate access rights** to that user's account or group (1).

flowchart LR
  C1[Client PC] --> SRV[Server running a NOS]
  C2[Client laptop] --> SRV
  C3[Client tablet] --> SRV
  SRV --> F[Shared files]
  SRV --> PR[Network printer]
  SRV --> DB[Shared database]
blocks.caption: Clients use resources managed by the network OS on the server

blocks.content: An OS that **collects jobs with similar requirements into groups (batches)** and processes them **one after another, automatically, without user interaction**, usually at a scheduled time.

items.title: Features
items.content:
- Jobs with similar requirements are **batched together** and run as a group.
- Data is **collected over a period of time** (a day, a week, a month) and then processed together.
- **No interaction** with the user while the jobs run — instructions are given in advance (job control language / scripts).
- Data is often **sorted before processing** (e.g. by account number).
- Usually runs at **off-peak times** (at night) when the computer is otherwise idle.
- Suited to **large volumes** of similar data.

items.title: Typical uses
items.content:
- **Payroll** — all salaries calculated at the end of the month.
- **Bank statements** and **utility bills** (electricity, water) printed for all customers.
- **Exam results** processing.
- Processing **cheques** or end-of-day sales records.

blocks.content:
flowchart TB
  J[Jobs collected during the day] --> B[Grouped into a batch and sorted]
  B --> R[Run automatically at night, no user input]
  R --> O[Output: bills, payslips, reports]
blocks.caption: Batch processing

blocks.title: Batch processing — advantages and disadvantages
rows: Results are **not immediate** — there is a delay
An error in one job may only be found after the whole batch runs
No interaction — jobs cannot be changed while running
Repetitive jobs are done the same way every time
Not suitable when up-to-date information is needed

theory.title: Choosing an OS type and exam practice

blocks.title: Which type of OS?
rows: Must respond to sensors within milliseconds
School network with 300 pupils sharing files and printers
Central user accounts, access rights, shared resources
A bank printing monthly statements for 2 million customers
Large volume of similar jobs, no interaction needed
A university mainframe used by hundreds of researchers at once
Many users share one powerful computer
A pupil's laptop running a browser, music and a word processor
One user, several programs at once
A digital watch or a simple calculator

blocks.title: Exam-style answers
blocks.content:
**Q: Explain two functions of an operating system. [2]**
1. **Memory management** — allocates RAM to programs and prevents them from overwriting each other's data (1).
2. **Processor management** — schedules processes so that several programs can share the CPU (multitasking) (1).

**Q: Give two features of the batch operating system. [2]**
Jobs with similar requirements are **batched together** and run as a group (1). Data is **collected over a period of time** and processed **without user interaction** (1).

**Q: Describe one feature of a real-time operating system. [2]**
It processes inputs **within a guaranteed time** (1) so that it can control a physical process **immediately**, e.g. inflating an airbag (1).

**Q: Compare single-tasking and multitasking operating systems. [2]**
A single-tasking OS runs **only one program at a time**, **whereas** a multitasking OS runs **several programs at once** by giving each a **time slice** of the CPU (1). Multitasking keeps the CPU busier but **needs more memory** (1).

- Confusing **multi-user** (many people) with **multitasking** (many programs).
- Saying a multitasking OS runs programs "at exactly the same time" on one core — it **switches** between them very quickly.
- Describing real-time as "fast". The key idea is a **guaranteed response within a deadline**.
- Writing "the OS manages memory" without saying **what** it does (allocate, protect, free).
- Thinking batch processing involves the user — it runs **without** user interaction.

Explain how time slicing makes multitasking possible.
Give three features of an RTOS and two examples of hard real-time systems.
How does a NOS manage user accounts?
Give two features, one advantage and one disadvantage of batch processing.

questions.title: Define an operating system
questions.text: Define the term **operating system**.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- System software that manages the computer's hardware and software resources (1)
- and provides a user interface / a platform for applications to run (1)

points.criterion: System software that manages hardware / resources
Provides a user interface or a platform for applications

scheme.model_answer: System software that manages the computer's hardware and software resources and provides a platform on which applications run.

questions.title: Not a function of the OS
questions.text: Which of the following is **not** a function of an operating system?

options.content: Calculating the totals in a spreadsheet

scheme.mark_scheme: C
scheme.explanation: Calculating totals is done by the spreadsheet application. The OS manages memory, processes and files.

questions.title: Match OS functions
questions.text: Match each function of an operating system to what the OS does.

right.text: Allocates RAM to each program and stops programs overwriting each other's data
Decides which process uses the CPU and for how long
Saves, names, moves and deletes files in folders
Checks user names and passwords and sets access rights

scheme.mark_scheme: Memory–R1, Processor–R2, File–R3, Security–R4. One mark per correct match.

questions.title: Memory management
questions.text: Describe how an operating system manages **memory**.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Any two (1 each):
- Allocates memory / RAM to programs and data when they are loaded
- Frees / deallocates memory when a program closes
- Protects memory so one program cannot access / overwrite another's memory
- Uses virtual memory when RAM is full / moves pages between RAM and disk
- Keeps track of which parts of memory are in use
scheme.model_answer: It allocates RAM to each program when it is loaded and frees it when the program closes, and it protects each program's memory so that other programs cannot overwrite it.

questions.title: Virtual memory
questions.text: Explain why an operating system uses **virtual memory**.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- When RAM is full, part of secondary storage / the disk is used as if it were RAM (1)
- so more programs / larger programs can run than would fit in RAM / the computer does not crash when RAM is full (1)

points.criterion: Part of the disk is used as an extension of RAM
So more / larger programs can run when RAM is full

scheme.model_answer: When RAM is full, the OS uses part of the hard disk as if it were extra RAM, so that more programs can stay open than would fit in main memory.

questions.title: Input/output management
questions.text:
Complete the sentences.

The OS communicates with each hardware device through a device [[1]]. Data travelling between the fast CPU and a slow printer is held temporarily in a [[2]]. When a device needs the CPU's attention, it sends an [[3]] signal.

scheme.mark_scheme: (1) driver (2) buffer (3) interrupt
scheme.explanation: Drivers translate OS commands for a device; buffers hold data between devices of different speeds; interrupts signal that a device needs attention.

questions.title: Booting
questions.text: During booting, which program copies the operating system kernel from secondary storage into RAM?

scheme.mark_scheme: B
scheme.explanation: The BIOS/UEFI runs the POST and then the bootstrap loader, which loads the OS kernel into RAM.

questions.title: Single-user vs multi-user
questions.text: Give **two** differences between a single-user and a multi-user operating system.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Any two (1 each), both sides stated or clearly implied:
- Single-user allows one user at a time; multi-user allows many users at the same time
- Multi-user shares CPU time / memory / storage between users (time-sharing); single-user gives all resources to one user
- Multi-user needs stronger security to keep users' data separate
- Single-user runs on PCs / laptops; multi-user on mainframes / servers
- Multi-user is more complex / expensive
scheme.model_answer: 1 A single-user OS allows only one user at a time, whereas a multi-user OS lets many users use the computer at the same time. 2 A multi-user OS must share the processor and memory fairly between the users and keep their data separate.

questions.title: Multi-user or multitasking
questions.text: A laptop that runs a browser, a music player and a word processor at the same time for one person is using a **multi-user** operating system.

scheme.mark_scheme: False.
scheme.explanation: One person running several programs is single-user multitasking. Multi-user means many people using the computer at the same time.

options.content: A university mainframe used by hundreds of researchers at once
A Linux server that many employees log in to remotely

questions.title: How multitasking works
questions.text: A computer has a single-core processor. Explain how a multitasking operating system makes several programs **appear** to run at the same time.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Any three (1 each):
- The CPU can only execute one process at a time
- The scheduler gives each process a short time slice (e.g. round robin / by priority)
- When the time slice ends the OS saves the state of the process and loads the next one (context switch)
- Switching happens many times per second, so all programs appear to run simultaneously

points.criterion: Only one process runs on the CPU at a time
Each process is given a time slice by the scheduler
Rapid switching / context switch makes them appear simultaneous

scheme.model_answer: The single CPU can only run one process at any moment. The scheduler gives each process a short time slice; when it ends, the OS saves that process's state and switches to the next one. This switching happens so quickly, many times a second, that all the programs seem to run at the same time.

questions.title: Define a real-time OS
questions.text: Define the term **real-time operating system**.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- An OS that processes inputs / responds within a guaranteed / fixed (very short) time / deadline (1)
- so that it can control a physical process / system as it happens (1)

points.criterion: Responds within a guaranteed time / deadline
To control a process / system immediately

scheme.model_answer: An operating system that processes inputs and responds within a guaranteed, very short time, so that it can control a physical system as events happen.

questions.title: Hard or soft real-time
questions.text: Tick (✓) **one** box in each row to show whether each system is **hard** real-time or **soft** real-time.

scheme.mark_scheme: Airbag → Hard (1); Video streaming → Soft (1); Pacemaker → Hard (1); Online game → Soft (1)
scheme.explanation: If a hard real-time deadline is missed the system fails and people may be hurt; a missed soft deadline only lowers quality.

questions.title: Features of an RTOS
questions.text: Describe **two** features of a real-time operating system.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): guaranteed response within a deadline; predictable / deterministic timing; priority-based pre-emptive scheduling — urgent tasks interrupt others; continuous monitoring of sensors with feedback; high reliability / fault tolerance / runs continuously; small and efficient / minimal user interface / embedded
scheme.model_answer: 1 It responds to inputs within a guaranteed deadline. 2 It uses priority scheduling, so the most urgent task can interrupt less important ones.

questions.title: Why an airbag needs an RTOS
questions.text: Explain why the airbag system in a car must use a real-time operating system.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- The airbag must inflate within a few milliseconds of the crash sensor detecting a collision / within a guaranteed time (1)
- otherwise it would inflate too late and the driver could be injured / it is safety-critical (1)

points.criterion: Response within a guaranteed (very short) time is needed
Linked to safety: a late response could injure people

scheme.model_answer: The airbag must inflate within milliseconds of the sensor detecting a crash; if the response were late, the airbag would be useless and the driver could be injured.

Guaranteed response to sensors within milliseconds
Sharing files and printers between client computers
Running only one program at a time

questions.title: NOS and user accounts

[Max 2] 1 mark for mentioning authentication / authorisation

questions.title: Features of batch processing

scheme.model_answer: 1 Jobs with similar requirements are grouped into a batch and run together. 2 The batch runs without any user interaction, often at night.

questions.title: Batch and the user

questions.title: Why batch for electricity bills
questions.text: An electricity company produces bills for 800 000 customers at the end of every month. Explain why batch processing is suitable for this task.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Any two (1 each):
- Large volume of similar jobs / every bill is calculated the same way
- Meter readings can be collected during the month and processed together
- Bills are not needed immediately / only once a month
- Can run automatically at night / off-peak without an operator

points.criterion: Results not needed immediately / can run without interaction at off-peak times

scheme.model_answer: There is a very large number of similar bills that are all calculated in the same way, and they are only needed once a month, so the readings can be collected and processed together automatically at night.

questions.title: Batch vs real-time
questions.text: Compare batch processing with real-time processing.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Any two (1 each), both sides needed:
- Batch processes data later in groups, whereas real-time processes data immediately as it arrives
- Batch has no user interaction during processing, whereas real-time responds to inputs continuously
- Batch suits large volumes where results are not urgent (bills), whereas real-time suits control / urgent systems (airbag, booking)
scheme.model_answer: Batch processing collects data and processes it later as a group without user interaction, whereas real-time processing handles each input immediately. Batch suits large non-urgent jobs such as monthly bills, while real-time suits control systems such as an airbag.

questions.title: Operating systems in a hospital
questions.text:
A hospital uses computers for three jobs:

- **Job 1** monitors patients' heart rates in intensive care and sounds an alarm immediately if there is a problem.
- **Job 2** lets 600 staff log in from any computer and open shared patient records.
- **Job 3** produces a report of every patient's medicines each night.

Identify the type of operating system or processing most suitable for **two** of the jobs and justify your choices.

scheme.mark_scheme:
For each of two jobs: type (1) + justification (1).
- Job 1: real-time (1) — must respond within a guaranteed time / safety-critical, a delayed alarm could cost a life (1)
- Job 2: network OS (1) — central user accounts / authentication / access rights to shared records for many users (1)
- Job 3: batch (1) — large volume of similar records, not urgent, run overnight without interaction (1)
[Max 4]

points.criterion: Correct type for the first job
Correct type for the second job

scheme.model_answer: Job 1 needs a real-time OS, because the alarm must sound within a guaranteed time and a delay could endanger the patient. Job 2 needs a network OS, because it manages the 600 user accounts centrally and gives each member of staff access rights to the shared records.
scheme.ai_instructions: Mark the best two jobs. A justification only scores if it matches the chosen type.

questions.title: Systems at an airport
questions.text: An international airport uses several computer systems: radar that tracks aircraft, staff computers connected to a central server, and a system that calculates all staff salaries at the end of each month.

- so controllers see up-to-date positions and collisions are avoided / safety-critical (1)

points.criterion: Data processed within a guaranteed time

scheme.model_answer: Aircraft positions change every second and must be processed immediately, so that controllers always see the current positions and can prevent collisions.

parts.title: Network OS features
parts.text: The central server runs a network operating system. State **two** features of the network operating system.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): user account management / authentication; access rights / authorisation; file sharing; printer sharing; centralised backup; security / firewall / logging; remote administration; supports many users at once
scheme.model_answer: 1 It authenticates staff when they log in to their accounts. 2 It lets staff share files and printers on the network.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Salaries of all staff are similar jobs that are calculated together once a month (1)
- results are not needed immediately, so the batch can run automatically without interaction / overnight (1)
scheme.model_answer: All the salaries are similar calculations that are only needed once a month, so they can be grouped and processed together automatically overnight.

questions.title: Comparing OS types
questions.text:
A company is choosing operating systems for: the laptops of its employees, its central server used by 200 staff at once, and the controller of a machine on its production line.

Compare single-user, multi-user, multitasking and real-time operating systems, and recommend a suitable type for **each** of the three uses.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Comparison points (max 4):
- single-user: one user at a time; multi-user: many users share resources at once (1)
- multitasking: several programs share the CPU using time slices (1)
- real-time: guaranteed response within a deadline; priority scheduling (1)
- multi-user needs strong security / resource sharing; real-time minimal UI / high reliability (1)

Recommendations (max 2, need all three for 2, two for 1):
- laptops: single-user multitasking
- server: multi-user (network) OS
- machine controller: real-time

points.criterion: Valid comparison of single-user and multi-user
All three recommendations correct and justified

scheme.model_answer: A single-user OS allows one person to use the computer at a time, while a multi-user OS lets many people share one computer's processor, memory and storage at once, so it needs stronger security to keep their data apart. A multitasking OS runs several programs at once by giving each a time slice of the CPU. A real-time OS responds to inputs within a guaranteed deadline using priority scheduling, and usually has little user interface. The laptops should use a single-user multitasking OS so employees can run several programs; the server should use a multi-user network OS so 200 staff can log in and share resources; the machine controller needs a real-time OS because it must react to sensors immediately.

questions.title: A pupil's laptop
questions.text: Madina uses her laptop to write an essay while music plays and a file downloads in the background.

parts.title: Memory management
parts.text: Describe how the operating system manages **memory** while these programs are running.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): allocates RAM to each program; protects each program's memory from the others; frees memory when a program closes; uses virtual memory if RAM is full; keeps track of used and free memory
scheme.model_answer: It gives each of the three programs its own part of RAM and stops them from overwriting each other's memory; if RAM becomes full it uses virtual memory on the disk.

parts.title: Multitasking
parts.text: The laptop has a single-core processor. Explain how the operating system allows the three programs to run at the same time.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Any three (1 each):
- It is a multitasking OS
- The CPU runs only one process at a time
- The scheduler gives each program a time slice
- The OS saves the state of one process and loads the next (context switch)
- Switching is so fast that the programs appear to run simultaneously
scheme.model_answer: The multitasking OS gives each program a short time slice of the CPU in turn. When a slice ends it saves that program's state and switches to the next one, and it does this so quickly that the essay, the music and the download all appear to run at the same time.

parts.title: Other OS functions
parts.text: Describe **two** other functions of the operating system, apart from memory management and multitasking.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each), described: file management; input/output / peripheral management through drivers; security / user accounts / access rights; providing a user interface; error handling; loading and running applications; handling interrupts
scheme.model_answer: 1 File management — it saves Madina's essay in a folder and records where it is stored on the disk. 2 It provides a graphical user interface so she can open programs with the mouse.
scheme.ai_instructions: Do not credit memory management or processor scheduling. A function name alone with no description is not enough.

questions.title: Types of operating system
questions.text: Different computer systems need different types of operating system.

parts.title: Which type
parts.text: Tick (✓) **one** box in each row to show the most suitable type of operating system.

prefill: Producing all customers' water bills at the end of the month
Controlling the engine temperature of an aircraft
Managing shared folders and printers for 50 office computers

scheme.mark_scheme: Water bills → Batch (1); Aircraft engine → Real-time (1); Office folders and printers → Network (1)

parts.title: Single-user vs multi-user
parts.text: Compare single-user and multi-user operating systems.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each), both sides needed: one user at a time vs many users simultaneously; all resources for one user vs resources shared between users (time-sharing); simpler security vs strong security to separate users' data; PC / laptop vs mainframe / server
scheme.model_answer: A single-user OS lets only one person use the computer at a time, whereas a multi-user OS lets many people use it at once. The multi-user OS must share CPU time and memory between the users and keep each user's data secure.

parts.title: Batch features
parts.text: Give **two** features of the batch operating system.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): jobs with similar requirements are batched together and run as a group; data collected for a defined period and processed as a pack; sorting is performed before processing; no user interaction; runs at off-peak / scheduled times
scheme.model_answer: 1 Jobs with similar requirements are grouped together and run as one batch. 2 The jobs run without any interaction with the user.

questions.title: Real-time systems in a car
questions.text: A modern car contains several embedded computers, including the airbag controller and the anti-lock braking system (ABS). Both use a real-time operating system.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Processes inputs / responds within a guaranteed time / deadline (1)
- to control a system as events happen (1)

points.criterion: Controls a system as events happen

scheme.model_answer: An OS that processes inputs and responds within a guaranteed time so that it can control a system as events happen.

parts.title: Why hard real-time
parts.text: The airbag controller is a **hard** real-time system. Explain what this means.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Every deadline must be met / response must always be within the time limit (1)
- missing a deadline means system failure / could injure the passengers (1)

points.criterion: Missing one is a failure / dangerous

scheme.model_answer: The airbag must always respond within its deadline; if it ever responds late, the system has failed and the passengers could be injured.

parts.title: RTOS features
parts.text: Describe **two** features of a real-time operating system, other than its response time.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): priority-based pre-emptive scheduling; deterministic / predictable; continuous monitoring of sensors with feedback; high reliability / fail-safe / runs continuously; small / efficient / embedded in ROM; minimal user interface
scheme.model_answer: 1 It uses priority scheduling, so the most urgent task interrupts others. 2 It is highly reliable and runs continuously without failing.
scheme.ai_instructions: Do not credit 'responds quickly / within a deadline' — it is excluded by the question.

parts.title: Soft real-time example
parts.text: The car's navigation and music screen is a **soft** real-time system. Explain the difference between hard and soft real-time systems, using the car as an example.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- In a soft real-time system a missed deadline only reduces quality / is not dangerous, e.g. the music or map updates late (1)
- In a hard real-time system a missed deadline is a failure / dangerous, e.g. the airbag / ABS (1)

points.criterion: Soft: missed deadline reduces quality, with car example
Hard: missed deadline is failure / dangerous, with car example

scheme.model_answer: If the navigation screen misses a deadline, the map just updates a little late, which is annoying but not dangerous. If the airbag or ABS misses a deadline, the system fails and people could be hurt.

questions.title: A school network and a bank
questions.text: A school has 300 computers connected to a server that runs a **network operating system**. A local bank uses **batch processing** to produce customers' monthly statements.

parts.title: User account management
parts.text: Describe how the network operating system implements **user account management**.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Any two (1 each): provides authentication and authorisation mechanisms; ensures that only authorised users can access network resources; verifies user identities (user name / password) at log-in; assigns appropriate access rights to users / groups
[Max 2]
scheme.model_answer: The NOS checks each pupil's user name and password when they log in and then gives their account the access rights for their group, so only authorised users can open each shared resource.

parts.title: Other NOS features
parts.text: State **two** other features of a network operating system.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): file sharing; printer sharing / print queues; centralised backup; security / firewall / activity logs; remote administration / software updates for clients; network services (DHCP, DNS, e-mail)
scheme.model_answer: 1 It lets pupils share files stored on the server. 2 It backs up all the users' work centrally.
scheme.ai_instructions: Do not credit user accounts / authentication again.

parts.title: Why batch for statements
parts.text: Explain why batch processing is suitable for producing the monthly statements.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): large number of similar jobs; transactions collected during the month and processed together; statements not needed immediately; can run automatically at night / off-peak without interaction
scheme.model_answer: Every customer's statement is a similar job, and the transactions collected during the month are only needed once a month, so they can be processed together automatically overnight.

parts.title: Disadvantage of batch
parts.text: Explain **one** disadvantage of batch processing for the bank.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Disadvantage (1) + explanation (1), e.g.
- Results are not immediate (1) so balances / statements are out of date until the batch runs (1)
- An error may only be found after the whole batch has been processed (1) so all statements may have to be produced again (1)
- No interaction during processing (1) so a job cannot be corrected while running (1)
scheme.model_answer: The results are not immediate, so a customer's statement does not show transactions until the batch has been run at the end of the month.
